text:
acme-sre: Hey team — deploying Redwood Private into our VPC. pip installs to fetch the runtime packages and model pulls from your registry are failing behind our egress filter. Error during model pull: 'ssl.SSLError: [SSL: TLSV1_ALERT_PROTOCOL_VERSION] tlsv1 alert protocol version'. Any quick checks?

maria-support: Sorry you're blocked. Can you paste the small repro steps and a minimal log snippet? Also, do you have an outbound HTTP proxy or MITM TLS inspection device? Those often cause SSL protocol errors.

acme-sre: Repro: fresh Ubuntu 22.04 VM in our private subnet, no proxy env set. Steps: `pip install redwood-cli` times out; `curl -v https://registry.redwood-inference.com/v1/models/health` shows TLS handshake failing. Snippet:
```
> GET /v1/models/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: registry.redwood-inference.com
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS header, Certificate Status (22):
* OpenSSL SSL_read: TLSv1 alert protocol version, errno 0
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) OpenSSL SSL_read: TLSv1 alert protocol version
```

maria-support: Thanks. Two likely culprits: 1) Egress firewall doing TLS terminate/inspect without proper SNI passthrough or using old TLS versions, 2) OCSP/CRL or CA verification blocked. For Redwood Private we rely on SNI & real endpoint certificate verification and OCSP can be requested during handshake. Please try an s_client test from the VM: `openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername registry.redwood-inference.com -status` and paste output.

acme-sre: Ran it — shows timeout waiting for OCSP response and then TLS alert. Full connect stalls on "OCSP Response: no response received".

ryan-ops: That matches an egress allowlist issue. A few practical notes:
- Don't only allow IPs; many endpoints are behind CDNs (CloudFront, Fastly) and IPs change. Allowlist by FQDN/SNI where possible.
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to the hostnames below and allow DNS resolution (UDP/TCP 53).
- OCSP/CRL endpoints are frequently on different hostnames (e.g., ocsp.digicert.com). Those need egress to validate cert chains.

lisa-eng: Minimal hosts we've seen break installs and model pulls if blocked: (allow egress to these FQDNs on port 443)
- registry.redwood-inference.com
- auth.redwood-inference.com
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com
- packages.redwood-inference.com
- apt.redwood-inference.com
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- model-cdn.redwood-inference.com (CNAMES to CloudFront)
- s3.amazonaws.com and *.s3.amazonaws.com (for model artifacts)
- *.cloudfront.net (models can be delivered via CDN)
Plus OCSP/CRL endpoints from major CAs, e.g.:
- ocsp.digicert.com
- ocsp.globalsign.com
- crl3.digicert.com

maria-support: Quick checklist to validate on your side:
1) From the VM, run: `dig +short registry.redwood-inference.com` and `curl -v --resolve registry.redwood-inference.com:443:<IP_FROM_DIG> https://registry.redwood-inference.com/v1/health` to bypass DNS and test connectivity to a particular IP.
2) Test SNI: `openssl s_client -connect <IP>:443 -servername registry.redwood-inference.com -status` — if that fails but `openssl s_client -connect <IP>:443 -servername <cdn-cname>` succeeds, you have SNI rewriting or a mismatch.
3) Ensure outbound TCP/UDP 53 to your DNS resolver is allowed (some middleboxes block DNS causing resolution to fail intermittently).
4) Confirm OCSP/CRL endpoints are reachable over 80/443.

acme-sre: We tried dig and IP connect; IP connects but s_client still waits for OCSP and then errors. We were only allowing registry.redwood-inference.com IPs previously and forgot OCSP hosts and CDNs.

ryan-ops: That explains it. Also note package installs hit files.pythonhosted.org and pypi.org. apt pulls will contact apt.redwood-inference.com and sometimes a mirror CDN. If you have strict allowlist rules, add wildcard CNAMES where possible and allowlisted OCSP endpoints.

maria-support: Here's a suggested allowlist (hostname-based):
- registry.redwood-inference.com (TCP/443)
- auth.redwood-inference.com (TCP/443)
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com (TCP/443)
- packages.redwood-inference.com, apt.redwood-inference.com (TCP/80,443)
- pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org (TCP/443)
- model hosting: *.s3.amazonaws.com, *.cloudfront.net, s3.amazonaws.com (TCP/443)
- OCSP/CRL: ocsp.digicert.com, ocsp.globalsign.com, crl3.digicert.com (TCP/80 or 443 depending on CA)
- DNS: allow UDP/TCP 53 to your resolver or to public resolvers if used temporarily

Also: If your egress appliance supports TLS SNI-based allowlisting, prefer that to fixed IPs. If it rewrites SNI or intercepts TLS with a local cert, you must add the interception device CA to the VM trust store — but Redwood's client expects real cert chains for integrity.

acme-sre: We'll add those hostnames and allow OCSP endpoints. One question: model artifact traffic sometimes hits upload.redwood-inference.com — should we allow that too?

lisa-eng: Yes, add upload.redwood-inference.com and model-cdn.redwood-inference.com. Also allow ephemeral ranges for some CDN providers; if possible, allow *.cloudfront.net rather than IPv4 ranges.

acme-sre: Added all suggested hostnames + OCSP endpoints and opened DNS. After a redeploy, pip installs succeeded and model pulls completed. Thanks! :tada:

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-17T11:15:02Z succeeded (was failing: redwood-private bootstrap).

maria-support: Great — closing the loop. For docs + KB, we'll share a short egress checklist linking these hosts and example openssl/curl tests. If you run into intermittent failures later, please capture `openssl s_client -status` output and we can advise further.

acme-sre: Will do. Appreciate the quick help!
